correctness.rationale: Connectedness gives an \((n-1)\)-simplex in \(\mathbf1^\perp\) with centroid zero. Regularity gives every vertex squared norm \(k(k+1)\), and the centroid average of squared distances proves the unique circumcenter and radius. For every \(x\in\mathbf1^\perp\), \(L^+x+\mathbf1/n\) is exactly the barycentric-coordinate vector, so the opposite-facet normal is \(L^+e_i\). Vertex transitivity makes these normal norms equal; the Frobenius/spectral trace gives their exact common square. Summing all barycentric clearances proves the inradius bound and forces the unique center at equality.

value.rationale: Laplacian simplices are a natural graph-polytope family whose established invariants are primarily lattice and Ehrhart theoretic. The result supplies an all-vertex-transitive Euclidean metric theorem with two complementary graph controls: degree alone fixes the circumradius, while the reciprocal fourth Laplacian spectral moment fixes the inradius. The pseudoinverse facet equation also gives a reusable bridge between graph spectral data and simplex metric geometry, applicable to broad families such as cycles, complete graphs, hypercubes, Cayley graphs, and distance-transitive graphs.
